required_inputs: Address candidates; jurisdiction; property type; authoritative parcel/building/unit identifiers; geometry relationships; buyer-confirmed selection where ambiguous.
applicability: Every property assessment. NOT_APPLICABLE is not permitted for property identity.
predicate: ASSESSED only when the selected property is resolved at the granularity needed by dependent checks. Multiple plausible units, unresolved parcel relations or conflicting identifiers fail this prerequisite.
evidence_output: Canonical identity and matched source identifiers, or preserved candidates and the exact unresolved relationship. Dependent conclusions cannot be attributed to an unconfirmed property.
action_priority: 0 for resolved identity. Null substantive priority for an unresolved identity; investigate through the gap task.
gap_policy: State NOT_ASSESSED; reason UNRESOLVED_PROPERTY_ID or CONFLICTED; substantive priority null; gap priority 3. Never transfer neighbouring-unit or building evidence silently.
next_action: Confirm the correct unit, parcel and building against authoritative records and the buyer's intended property, then rerun dependent checks.
limitations: A shared address coordinate is not proof of shared title, dwelling condition or hazard exposure. This is a workflow policy, not a risk probability.

required_inputs: Source contract; acquisition result; schema/parser validation; field units; geographic and time coverage; permitted uses; check criticality; required-input manifest.
applicability: Every required source-dependent check. Missing access or evidence does not make the underlying check NOT_APPLICABLE.
predicate: A dependent check can become ASSESSED only if acquisition or permitted retained evidence is usable, required fields and units validate, coverage includes the requested scope, and the intended use is authorised. An empty response is usable negative evidence only after these gates pass.
evidence_output: Explicit source-check outcome with coverage, query period, parser version, rights policy and rejected or quarantined fields.
action_priority: 0 for a passed quality gate; null substantive priority when the gate fails. The gate does not itself assert a physical property hazard.
gap_policy: State NOT_ASSESSED; reason MISSING_INPUT, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, OUTSIDE_COVERAGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, UNIT_UNKNOWN or LICENCE_NOT_AUTHORISED. Gap priority 3 for a critical check, 2 for another required check, 1 for an optional check.
next_action: Repair or replace the source path, resolve units/coverage/rights, or retain the visible limitation. Recalculate only the affected checks after valid evidence arrives.
limitations: A publicly readable URL is not sufficient permission for every storage or display use. A successful HTTP request alone does not establish coverage or a negative property finding.

required_inputs: Source-specific freshness policy; effective/observation date; publication and retrieval dates; current-version or supersession evidence; quote/document expiry where applicable.
applicability: Every time-sensitive source or document. A historical assessment uses the applicable historical policy and available source version.
predicate: Evidence passes when it meets its source-specific currency requirements and is not superseded for the assessed question. An old model publication date alone does not fail a map confirmed as the current official designation.
evidence_output: Source vintage, last currency check, applicable expiry/version and the reason it is current, historical-current, or stale for this use.
action_priority: 0 when the currency gate passes; null substantive priority when it fails.
gap_policy: State NOT_ASSESSED; reason STALE or PUBLICATION_TIME_UNKNOWN. Gap priority follows required-check criticality: 3 critical, 2 other required, 1 optional. A retained older result stays dated and cannot masquerade as a current result.
next_action: Obtain the current applicable version or explicitly limit the assessment/replay claim. Preserve previous versions and supersession history.
limitations: Currency policy is explicit and source-specific. Polling an annual source daily does not create daily observations. Unknown publication time limits faithful historical replay.

required_inputs: Validated parcel/building/source geometries; coordinate reference systems; positional accuracy; relevant boundary relation; vertical datums if elevation comparison is requested.
applicability: Any check whose conclusion depends on geometry, distance, overlap or elevation. A vertical-datum gate applies only to analyses requiring vertical comparison.
predicate: The spatial gate fails when invalid or insufficient geometry, unresolved coordinate systems, relevant positional uncertainty spanning the boundary, or incompatible vertical datums prevent the requested conclusion.
evidence_output: Separate parcel, dwelling and access relations; method and units; uncertain boundary zone; exact comparison that could not be completed.
action_priority: 0 when the required spatial relation is sufficiently established; null substantive priority for the blocked conclusion. A boundary touch never silently becomes a clear result.
gap_policy: State NOT_ASSESSED; reason INSUFFICIENT_SPATIAL_PRECISION, GEOMETRY_INVALID or DATUM_UNRESOLVED. Gap priority 3 for a critical consequence check, otherwise 2. Retain any narrower relation that is sufficiently assessed.
next_action: Obtain suitable geometry, survey/elevation information or an appropriate site assessment; rerun only the affected spatial checks.
limitations: A point or parcel centroid is not a building footprint. A universal search radius is not an impact model. No distance or height conclusion is emitted in unknown units.

required_inputs: Resolved parcel; current applicable official flood-extent scenario; verified coverage; validated overlap relation with sufficient spatial precision; separate dwelling/access evidence where available; any reviewed resolution record.
applicability: Properties within the supported flood-screen jurisdiction and requested screening scope. Missing coverage is handled by FL02 and is not NOT_APPLICABLE.
predicate: After identity, quality, currency and spatial gates pass, a positive parcel/flood-scenario overlap triggers mapped exposure. A boundary-only or uncertainty-spanning case is routed to GE01 instead of forcing inside/outside classification.
evidence_output: The exact official scenario and mapped parcel relation, with dwelling, access and consequence assessment states kept separate. Retain the designation even if a later professional review resolves the investigation task.
action_priority: 3 for unresolved positive overlap under the provisional due-diligence policy. 1 after appropriate current site/insurance evidence and an authorised review resolve the material questions; 0 for no overlap within fully assessed source scope. No unrelated flood mechanism is cleared.
gap_policy: Unusable required extent/identity evidence gives NOT_ASSESSED, null substantive priority and gap 3 with the applicable reason. Missing floor, drainage, access or insurance evidence leaves the supported overlap ASSESSED but creates separate consequence gaps, normally priority 3 when critical.
next_action: Obtain relevant dwelling-floor, drainage/access and insurance evidence; document specialist interpretation or mitigation and whether it resolves the specific buyer concern.
limitations: An extent intersection is not a numeric depth, annual damage probability, expected loss or proof that the dwelling will flood. Closing a task does not erase the underlying map designation.

required_inputs: Required flood-mechanism checklist for the scope; source coverage geometries and periods; successful query evidence; scenario definitions; exclusions and current-version status.
applicability: Every required flood-screen mechanism, including separate river and overland-flow checks where required by the versioned catalogue.
predicate: Coverage is insufficient when the source excludes the property, cannot be verified, is unavailable/stale, or does not address a required mechanism. A no-intersection result cannot pass without verified coverage.
evidence_output: Mechanism-by-mechanism coverage and explicitly unassessed mechanisms. A sufficiently assessed river result does not answer an overland-flow question.
action_priority: 0 for a passed coverage gate; null substantive priority for an unassessed mechanism, with a separate investigation task.
gap_policy: State NOT_ASSESSED; reason OUTSIDE_COVERAGE, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, STALE, MISSING_INPUT or UNSUPPORTED_METHOD as applicable; gap priority 3 for each critical required mechanism.
next_action: Identify a suitable source or obtain an appropriate site/drainage assessment. Keep the gap visible when no supported source can answer the question.
limitations: No source record is not the same as no risk. The rule concerns evidence coverage and does not establish that an unmapped property is hazardous.

required_inputs: Resolved relevant land/building geometry; current applicable official bushfire designation; verified coverage and spatial precision; appropriate building/site/insurance evidence for any task resolution.
applicability: Required bushfire screening in a supported jurisdiction. An unavailable designation layer remains an evidence gap.
predicate: After prerequisite gates pass, a positive overlap with the applicable official designation triggers a due-diligence action. An unresolved boundary relation routes to GE01.
evidence_output: Official category, version, location and property relation, with building vulnerability and insurance implications recorded as separate assessed or unassessed questions.
action_priority: 3 for unresolved positive overlap under the provisional workflow; 1 after current appropriate site/building/insurance evidence and authorised review resolve the material task; 0 for no designation overlap in fully assessed scope.
gap_policy: Unusable designation evidence gives NOT_ASSESSED, null substantive priority and critical gap 3. Missing vulnerability or cost evidence does not erase a valid designation finding; it creates a separate gap.
next_action: Review applicable property/building implications and suitable insurance terms with appropriate evidence, then record any supported resolution.
limitations: A designation is not a property-specific probability of fire, a forecast insurance premium or a conclusion about legal compliance. Site resolution does not remove an official designation.

required_inputs: Property-matched inspection or appropriately qualified assessment; inspection date and scope; defect description/materiality; exclusions; reviewed quotes/repair evidence where available; buyer requirements.
applicability: Building condition relevant to the proposed purchase and use. Hidden or uninspected components remain explicitly outside assessed scope.
predicate: A validated inspection identifies a material defect or recommended material investigation. Priority 4 requires appropriate evidence of a present conflict with an essential intended-use requirement, not merely an uncertain repair estimate.
evidence_output: Observed defect and scope, required investigation/repair, evidenced cost or unknown cost, and any supported repair completion or specialist resolution.
action_priority: 3 for an unresolved material defect or its material cost; 4 for a verified present essential-use conflict; 1 for a documented minor monitoring issue; 0 when no flag is identified in sufficiently inspected scope or a finding is validly resolved.
gap_policy: Missing/unsuitable inspection gives NOT_ASSESSED, reason MISSING_INPUT or INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, null substantive priority and gap 3 for required building due diligence. Missing cost leaves an observed defect ASSESSED and creates a separate cost gap; no invented quote.
next_action: Obtain scoped specialist assessment and quotation or completion evidence; record whether the evidence actually resolves the specific defect and buyer consequence.
limitations: Listing photos cannot establish the absence of concealed defects. A quote is not proof of completed repair. Costs remain ranges where scope is uncertain.

required_inputs: Property type and ownership structure; versioned required-document checklist; available inspections; relevant common-property, capital-works and levy records; document dates and authorised access scope.
applicability: Required building documents for every relevant property; strata/shared-liability checks only where that ownership relationship applies. Non-applicability needs an evidenced ownership reason.
predicate: A required document/scope item is missing, unusable or excludes a required component; or appropriate records identify a dated special levy or capital-work liability applicable to the buyer case.
evidence_output: Document coverage, exclusions, confirmed buyer-relevant levies/works and explicitly unresolved liability amounts or timing.
action_priority: 0 for complete reviewed scope without a flag; 2 for a known cost requiring an allowance; 3 for an unresolved material shared liability; 4 only when a verified current liability conflicts with a declared essential funding limit.
gap_policy: Missing required evidence gives NOT_ASSESSED with MISSING_INPUT, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, STALE or LICENCE_NOT_AUTHORISED; null substantive priority and gap 3 for critical items, 2 for other required items. Public-screen mode does not make documents irrelevant.
next_action: Obtain authorised missing records, clarify levy/work obligations and timing, and add supported costs once to the ownership scenario.
limitations: A building's total liability is not automatically the individual buyer's share. Absence of a recorded levy does not prove absence of future capital works.

required_inputs: Resolved property/title identity; applicable authoritative title/lease/strata/planning instrument; exact buyer intended use and essential requirements; qualified interpretation where required; effective dates.
applicability: Each declared intended use or essential ownership requirement. A missing buyer plan or instrument is not grounds for treating a relevant check as NOT_APPLICABLE.
predicate: Appropriate reviewed evidence establishes a current restriction that conflicts with a declared essential use. Ambiguous wording or conflicting instruments cannot establish the definitive conflict without resolution.
evidence_output: Exact restriction and source location, affected buyer requirement, effective period, reviewed interpretation and unresolved alternative or approval dependency.
action_priority: 4 for a verified present essential-use conflict; 3 for a potentially material unresolved legal/use question; 2 for a relevant non-essential constraint; 0 when the specific reviewed requirement has no identified conflict.
gap_policy: Missing, ambiguous or conflicting required evidence gives NOT_ASSESSED with MISSING_INPUT, CONFLICTED or INTERPRETATION_REQUIRED; null substantive priority and gap 3 for an essential-use/title question, otherwise 2.
next_action: Obtain appropriate professional confirmation, evidence of permissible alternatives or a revised buyer plan; create a new assessment version after resolution.
limitations: The engine does not certify legal compliance or invent approval rights. A contextual zoning label alone cannot settle a title, lease or permission question.

required_inputs: Current property-specific quote/policy terms; effective/expiry dates; declared buyer cover requirements; exclusions, excesses and insured limits; reviewed interpretation for ambiguous terms.
applicability: Any required assessment of insurance availability, affordability or suitability for the buyer's stated requirements.
predicate: Reviewed quote terms fail a stated essential cover requirement, or a material exclusion/limit remains unresolved. The tested subject is the reviewed quote, not availability across the entire insurance market.
evidence_output: Quote-specific cover fit, exclusions, excesses, known premium and affected buyer requirement; record alternatives separately.
action_priority: 4 for a verified present quote/essential-requirement conflict; 3 for material unresolved cover; 2 for a non-essential cost/term requiring review; 0 for an evidenced acceptable current quote within reviewed scope.
gap_policy: Missing, expired or materially ambiguous quote evidence gives NOT_ASSESSED with MISSING_INPUT, STALE or INTERPRETATION_REQUIRED; null substantive priority and gap 3 when insurance is a critical required check.
next_action: Clarify the terms or obtain suitable alternative quotes, then reassess the exact cover and budget requirements.
limitations: One refusal or unsuitable quote does not prove general uninsurability. A quote does not guarantee future renewal terms or future claim payment.

required_inputs: Canonical project identity; source-backed milestones and plans; candidate geometry/use/height where available; property orientation and relationship; buyer amenity priorities and holding period.
applicability: Known nearby projects with a defensible potential relationship to sunlight, privacy, access, noise or competing supply. A generic radius alone retrieves candidates but does not establish impact.
predicate: A relevant project and geometry/use relationship support a specific potential impact, while sufficient impact modelling or source documentation has not yet resolved it.
evidence_output: Project stage and version, supported relevance, affected buyer outcome, known timeline and the exact unverified impact question.
action_priority: 2 for a supported potential amenity issue; 3 when a declared essential requirement could be materially affected and the critical impact evidence is unresolved; 1 for relevant context requiring monitoring only; 0 for no relevant candidate in a fully assessed search scope.
gap_policy: Missing register coverage or unusable project identity gives NOT_ASSESSED with OUTSIDE_COVERAGE, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE or UNRESOLVED_PROJECT_ID. Missing essential impact inputs create a separate gap 3; other required impact gaps receive 2.
next_action: Obtain the applicable plans/conditions and suitable shadow, noise or access evidence; preserve revised/cancelled project versions and rerun the impact check.
limitations: A proposal is not an approval, and approval is not completion. Northern location alone does not establish shadow loss; no price deduction is inferred from proximity.

required_inputs: Property-specific measurement or suitable validated impact model; proposed/as-built geometry and assumptions; project stage; declared buyer threshold and whether essential; relevant time window.
applicability: Only where a buyer or explicitly versioned review policy defines the amenity measure and threshold, and the available method can evaluate it.
predicate: The supported measured/modelled amenity falls below the stated threshold or exceeds a stated maximum. Current measured effects and conditional future-project effects are classified separately.
evidence_output: Measure, units, threshold, method, assumptions, project state, assessed period and the exact buyer requirement breach.
action_priority: 4 for a verified present measured conflict with an essential requirement; 3 for a supported conditional future breach of an essential requirement; 2 for a non-essential threshold breach; 0 for no breach in the adequately assessed scope.
gap_policy: Unsupported method, geometry or threshold gives NOT_ASSESSED with UNSUPPORTED_METHOD, INSUFFICIENT_SPATIAL_PRECISION or MISSING_INPUT; null substantive priority and gap 3 for an essential material question, otherwise 2.
next_action: Validate the impact with appropriate source plans or specialist evidence; review mitigation or revise the buyer requirement without overwriting historical findings.
limitations: Thresholds are declared preferences or visible workflow policy, not universal valuation rules. A future impact remains conditional even when the model arithmetic is reliable.

required_inputs: Defined comparable dwelling segment and substitute market; canonical deduplicated developments; net dwelling additions by stage; source dates/coverage; horizon; demand context; any explicit review threshold.
applicability: A market-context or resale/rental competition assessment with a declared relevant property segment and geography.
predicate: One or more evidenced net competing additions exist in the relevant pipeline. Deduplicate land release, DA, approval and construction records by project. A higher review action requires breach of an explicit recorded competition threshold or a separately specified material buyer dependency.
evidence_output: Existing stock/listings separately from proposal, approval, commencement and completion counts; net additions; horizon scenarios; demand indicators and coverage limits.
action_priority: 1 for an evidenced competing pipeline without a supported material threshold breach; 2 when a declared review threshold is exceeded; 0 only where the complete tested scope identifies no competing pipeline. No priority implies a price-loss probability.
gap_policy: Insufficient segmentation, deduplication, geographic coverage or stage evidence gives NOT_ASSESSED for the affected conclusion with MISSING_INPUT, OUTSIDE_COVERAGE or CONFLICTED; null substantive priority and gap 2, or 3 for an explicitly critical buyer dependency.
next_action: Reconcile project stages and net yields, obtain missing demand/completion evidence, and compare named low/base/high delivery scenarios without invented probabilities.
limitations: Pipeline is not completed supply; population is not household formation; territory totals do not establish suburb completions. The rule does not independently establish oversupply or a future price fall.

required_inputs: Recorded offence category counts; complete comparable periods; geography and boundary version; valid denominator for rates; suppression/reporting caveats; any explicit buyer or review-policy threshold.
applicability: Area-level crime context where the category and geography are relevant to a declared buyer concern. No personal offending profile is produced.
predicate: Report comparable category counts and, where justified, rates/trends. A threshold-based review action fires only when a recorded applicable threshold is exceeded on valid comparable data.
evidence_output: Counts, denominator and period; geographic resolution; rate/change where valid; small-count and reporting caveats; explicit threshold if one is used.
action_priority: 2 for a valid breach of a declared review threshold; otherwise 1 for relevant contextual observations. 0 may describe no flag under the specific assessed policy but never no crime risk at the house.
gap_policy: Missing coverage, incompatible periods/boundaries or invalid denominator gives NOT_ASSESSED for the affected comparison with OUTSIDE_COVERAGE, PERIOD_MISMATCH, BOUNDARY_MISMATCH or DENOMINATOR_INVALID; null substantive priority and gap 2 for a required comparison.
next_action: Obtain comparable official data or retain counts and limitations; investigate location-specific concerns using appropriate evidence rather than demographic proxies.
limitations: A suburb statistic is not an offence probability at the property. Small counts are not amplified into dramatic unsupported percentage conclusions. Protected demographic characteristics are not risk proxies.

required_inputs: Supported loan structure/repayment; net household income; precisely defined rental receipts where applicable; living and other debt costs; all required property costs; declared no-drawdown/reserve requirements; baseline horizon and cash schedule where needed.
applicability: Buyer financial assessment with sufficient budget inputs. A public screen without finances returns NOT_ASSESSED for affordability, not a reassuring financial score.
predicate: Calculate baseline monthly surplus with every deduction applied once. A negative baseline surplus triggers review. It becomes a confirmed requirement conflict only if a declared essential no-drawdown requirement is violated, or the baseline cash schedule breaches an essential reserve within the specified horizon.
evidence_output: Repayment, income, itemised costs, surplus/deficit, horizon and reserve schedule; input sources, exclusions and the exact declared requirement affected.
action_priority: 3 by default for a negative baseline surplus; 4 only for the verified essential no-drawdown/reserve conflict defined in the predicate. 0 for no baseline flag with complete inputs. Planned drawdown is not automatically a requirement conflict.
gap_policy: Missing budget/cost fields or unsupported loan structure gives NOT_ASSESSED with MISSING_INPUT or UNSUPPORTED_METHOD; null substantive priority and gap 3 for a required essential affordability check. A repayment-only calculation may still be displayed within its narrower scope.
next_action: Verify costs and loan assumptions, agree the relevant duration and drawdown tolerance, and revise the purchase/finance plan where a declared requirement is breached.
limitations: A submitted budget is not loan approval. Tax treatment, daily lender interest, fees and supported loan structures are explicit. No rate or income forecast is implied.

required_inputs: Validated baseline inputs; named rate/income/vacancy/cost scenario; scenario duration in months; cash after settlement and committed upfront costs; protected reserve or minimum surplus target; buyer tolerance and essentiality; monthly schedule.
applicability: A buyer-selected or clearly labelled policy scenario whose horizon and target are explicitly defined. No default occurrence probability is supplied.
predicate: Simulate the specified duration. Fire when minimum cash balance within that duration falls below the protected reserve, or a stated scenario surplus target is breached. A negative surplus whose duration ends before reserve breach must not be reported as an observed reserve breach.
evidence_output: Scenario assumptions and duration, monthly cash schedule, minimum balance, time to reserve if reached, target breaches and source/calculator versions.
action_priority: 3 when a named scenario required for purchase review breaches its declared reserve or surplus target; 2 for an optional exploratory scenario breach; 4 only when complete supported inputs establish conflict with an explicitly essential must-withstand requirement. 0 for no breach within the complete named scenario. Any priority 4 is a requirement conflict under the stated assumptions, not a forecast that the shock will occur.
gap_policy: Missing duration, target, cash or required cost inputs gives NOT_ASSESSED with MISSING_INPUT; null substantive priority and gap 3 for a required purchase-review scenario, otherwise 2. Do not assume an infinite stress duration.
next_action: Confirm assumptions and duration, examine revised finance/cost/reserve options, and show the resulting scenario difference without claiming the shock will occur.
limitations: Cash after settlement cannot be reused as deposit or committed repair funding. Joint shocks are explicit. Priority reflects the declared review/essential requirement; it does not imply the scenario is likely. No expected loss is calculated by summing or probability-weighting uncalibrated scenarios.

required_inputs: Cash available after settlement and committed upfront costs; buyer-declared minimum cash amount or buffer-month threshold; threshold units and essentiality; complete monthly essential outgoings for a months-based metric.
applicability: Only where the buyer or a visible accepted policy defines the buffer metric and threshold. No threshold is invented from general advice.
predicate: For an amount target, compare total remaining available cash with the declared minimum. For a months target, divide remaining cash by explicitly defined essential monthly outgoings and compare with the declared minimum months. Do not subtract the same protected amount before comparing it to itself.
evidence_output: Available cash, defined buffer metric, threshold, calculation and shortfall. Preserve whether the input is current or a proposed settlement configuration.
action_priority: 4 for a sufficiently verified present/configuration breach of an essential buyer buffer requirement; 2 for a non-essential review threshold breach; 0 for a satisfied declared threshold with complete inputs.
gap_policy: Missing cash, threshold or required denominator gives NOT_ASSESSED with MISSING_INPUT or DENOMINATOR_INVALID; null substantive priority and gap 3 for an essential requirement, otherwise 2. Zero outgoings do not produce an infinite safety claim.
next_action: Verify committed cash uses and outgoings; alter allocated cash or the buyer's explicitly recorded requirement if appropriate, then create a revised assessment.
limitations: Thresholds are buyer requirements or visible workflow policy, not universal financial suitability standards. The rule is distinct from FN02's time-varying stress resilience.

required_inputs: Proposed purchase price; known acquisition costs and committed immediate works; confirmed applicable loan funds; cash explicitly allocated to purchase; funding dates and conditions.
applicability: Buyer assessments that evaluate whether the submitted purchase configuration is funded.
predicate: Compute funding_gap = max(0, purchase price + known acquisition costs + committed immediate works - confirmed applicable loan funds - cash allocated to purchase). A positive gap on complete confirmed inputs is a present configuration conflict.
evidence_output: Itemised cash requirement, funding sources and conditions, gap amount and excluded or unknown costs. Preserve separate cash allocated to later reserves.
action_priority: 4 for a confirmed positive funding gap; 0 for no gap within a complete confirmed funding scope. Estimated or conditional unconfirmed finance cannot establish a fully funded conclusion.
gap_policy: Missing costs, uncertain cash allocation or unconfirmed loan availability gives NOT_ASSESSED with MISSING_INPUT or FUNDING_UNCONFIRMED; null substantive priority and gap 3. A provisional estimate can be shown but remains labelled provisional.
next_action: Confirm acquisition costs and loan/cash availability or revise the purchase configuration. Ensure cash is not simultaneously assigned to deposit, immediate work and emergency reserves.
limitations: This checks the submitted funding configuration, not lending eligibility or a guarantee of settlement. Amounts and dates may require verification before a binding decision.

required_inputs: Canonical project with source-backed milestones; supported route/service/amenity change; buyer destination or need; useful access evidence; expected time range, holding period, dependencies and adverse offsets.
applicability: A project or delivered service has a defensible relationship to a buyer benefit. Straight-line proximity alone is insufficient to claim a walking-time improvement.
predicate: Supported evidence identifies a specific useful benefit, its current/projected state and its relationship to the buyer's time horizon. Funding, approval, contracts and construction remain independent milestone facts.
evidence_output: Separate opportunity card stating benefit, supporting milestones, timing, horizon fit, dependencies and noise/construction/supply offsets. Delivered amenities are labelled current; future benefits stay conditional.
action_priority: Null in downside scoring: this is a separate opportunity result and never subtracts from assessed or gap priorities. Opportunity follow-up tasks may have their own explicit workflow ordering.
gap_policy: Unsupported benefit/status/timing produces NOT_ASSESSED for that claim with MISSING_INPUT, CONFLICTED or UNSUPPORTED_METHOD. Use an opportunity follow-up priority 2, or a separate critical gap 3 if an essential buyer requirement explicitly depends on the unverified service.
next_action: Verify the meaningful access/service benefit and delivery evidence; monitor specific milestones and recalculate if route, scope, timing or buyer needs change.
limitations: No invented delivery probability, automatic price uplift or assumption that benefits are unpriced. A future service can coexist with substantial construction or permanent amenity costs.
